_doc: How each boat is built on its stand (user 2026-09-29: 'a boat stand by the river, they bring materials, attach to it and see it grow into something real'; 'a puzzle: we have the pieces but need to do puzzles to complete it'; 'takes engineering work on the user to research'). BoatBuild reads it. hull: the shape (m): length, beam, depth of the hull, the sheer's rise at the ends and how far the ends draw to a point; the meshes are made from these numbers. stages, in the order the real craft goes: id, name, know (the survival knowledge id, SurvivalLearning; unknown = cannot be done, heard of / seen = done clumsily), needs (item ids and counts, brought to the stand), work_min (game minutes of work), tool (any of), puzzle (the skill game a stage plays, '' none yet), shows (the parts of the hull that appear), weight (how much its grade weighs for the boat), what (what the grade of it becomes in the finished boat). The order is the craft's own; the birchbark canoe goes inside-out (bed, skin, gunwales, then ribs, then seams), which is not how a plank boat goes.

birchbark.name: Birchbark canoe
birchbark.history: The Algonquian nations' bark canoe: built inside-out on a bed of stakes by the water, the skin sewn with spruce root, the gunwales pegged, the cedar ribs steamed in last, the seams sealed with pitch, tallow and charcoal. Light enough to carry over a portage; the canoe of the fur trade.

stages.name: Lay, shape and sew the bark
